At 1.8 K, the 𝐴* peak in the Te single crystal is approximately 66 times higher than the intrinsic P2 peak in MnTe
Raman spectra of MnTe(0001) and a Te(0001) single crystal, acquired at 300 and 1.8 K under identical experimental conditions.
CLM-MAT-0203.statement: The A1 peak in the Te single crystal is approximately 66 times higher in intensity than the intrinsic P2 peak in MnTe at 1.8 K.

extra_quotes: Raman measurements were performed in a backscattering geometry on the (0001) surface of MnTe single crystals using 632.8 nm excitation.
We measured SHG in reflection geometry on MnTe(0001) using 800-nm, 50-fs pulses incident at 45°, with the 400-nm signal analyzed in the S-out and P-out channels
P3 may be associated with local strain, which has been proposed as a possible origin of the Raman-mode splitting near 100 cm−1 in MnTe [24].
